metadata.title: Western Blot (SDS-PAGE → Transfer → Immunoblotting)
metadata.purpose: Separate proteins by SDS-PAGE, transfer them onto a membrane, and detect a target protein with a specific primary antibody and an enzyme-conjugated secondary antibody.
metadata.scope: Denaturing (SDS) western blot of soluble protein samples on a nitrocellulose membrane, developed by AP or HRP chromogenic/ECL detection. Not validated here for native PAGE, PVDF membranes, or quantitative fluorescent western blot.
metadata.estimatedTime: ~2 days (Day 1: gel + transfer + overnight block; Day 2: antibody incubations, washes, development)
beforeYouBegin: Design the blot first: which lanes report each tag, which lane is the input control, how the interaction is read out, and what controls are loaded.
Mix every sample with 2× SDS sample buffer at 1:1 (v/v) and denature before loading.
Prepare all buffers listed in Materials and Reagents.

materials.name: Filter paper
materials.specification: Cut to gel size, blotting grade

materials.name: Transfer buffer
materials.specification: 25 mM Tris, 200 mM glycine, 20% methanol, 0.1% SDS, pH 8.5
materials.rawText: Transfer Buffer: 25mmol/L Tris, 200mmol/L Glycine, 20% Methanol, 0.1%SDS, pH 8.5

materials.name: AP substrate (BCIP-T + NBT)
materials.specification: 35 uL BCIP-T (50 mg/mL in DMF) + 45 uL NBT (50 mg/mL in DMF) per 10 mL AP buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl, 100 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, pH 9.5)

materials.name: HRP substrate (CN/DAB, chromogenic)
materials.specification: 30 mg CN + 10 mg DAB, PBS to 50 mL; add 10 uL 30% H2O2 per 10 mL just before use

equipment.name: Vertical SDS-PAGE electrophoresis cell + power supply
Wet (tank) transfer apparatus
equipment.settings: Constant current I (mA) = gel area (cm^2) × 0.8 mA/cm^2; 40-60 min

steps.action: Treat all samples with 2× SDS sample buffer and denature.
steps.criticalNotes: Confirm the pull-down samples (tubes AB, CB) and the input sample.

steps.action: Load samples per the blot design.
steps.criticalNotes: Reserve a lane for MW ladder and for controls.

steps.action: Run the gel to separate proteins.
Remove the gel from the cassette; cut per design if needed.
(Optional) Stain a portion/duplicate gel with Coomassie R-250; destain later.
steps.criticalNotes: Use a second gel or cut the gel if both Coomassie and transfer are required.

steps.action: Soak 8 filter papers in transfer buffer; rinse the NC membrane.
steps.criticalNotes: Drive off all bubbles between layers.

steps.action: Assemble the stack in the tank: cathode(−) → filter paper → gel → NC membrane → filter paper → anode(+).
steps.criticalNotes: Protein migrates from gel toward the membrane on the anode side.

steps.action: Run constant-current transfer; then rinse membrane with TBS.
Block the membrane in block solution.
steps.criticalNotes: Choose overnight (4 degC) vs RT 1-2 h per optimized protocol.

steps.action: Wash membrane with fresh TBST; keep wet.

steps.criticalNotes: Match antibody to the tag being probed.
Use AP- or HRP-conjugate matching your substrate.

steps.action: Wash with TBS to remove Tween-20.

steps.criticalNotes: For HRP/DAB add H2O2 immediately before use.

steps.action: Stop development in ddH2O; dry membrane on filter paper.
steps.criticalNotes: Chromogenic band color fades over a few days — image promptly.

controls.name: Input control
controls.description: Load the input (T7-tag-B) sample to confirm expression/loading.

controls.name: Tag-specificity controls
controls.description: Probe Strep-tag lanes (A, C) with α-Strep and the input with α-T7.

controls.name: Interaction readout
controls.description: Compare pull-down lanes (AB vs CB) to test protein-protein interaction.

controls.name: Secondary-only control
controls.description: No-primary-antibody lane to detect non-specific secondary binding.

expectedOutputs: Discrete immunoreactive band(s) at the expected molecular weight for each tag.
Optional Coomassie gel showing total-protein loading.
A recorded image of the developed membrane (bands fade, so capture promptly).

troubleshooting.cause: Membrane dried; insufficient blocking; antibody too concentrated
troubleshooting.solution: Keep membrane wet; extend blocking; dilute antibody / add washes

troubleshooting.cause: Poor transfer; antibody too dilute; substrate exhausted
troubleshooting.solution: Verify transfer (Ponceau/Coomassie); increase antibody; use fresh substrate
Add protease inhibitors; ensure full denaturation; confirm antibody specificity
Re-roll the stack to remove bubbles before transfer

safety: Unpolymerized acrylamide is a neurotoxin — wear gloves; handle gels and stocks with care.
Methanol (transfer buffer) and DMF (substrate stocks) are flammable/toxic — use in a fume hood.
DAB is a suspected carcinogen; NBT/BCIP and H2O2 are irritants — follow institutional disposal rules.
limitations: Chromogenic detection is non-quantitative and fades; transfer efficiency for high-MW proteins is not addressed. Sample biosafety level depends on the source material.
